text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.47% today to $135.27, recovering modestly from a sharp drop two days earlier when the stock fell nearly 3% after climate talks collapsed without committing to phase out fossil fuels. The rebound reflects stabilization around current oil prices—US crude holding at $89.53 per barrel—rather than any new company-specific catalyst, though geopolitical tensions remain a backdrop with ongoing attacks on Saudi and Russian energy infrastructure.

The two-week decline of 1.88% sits against a backdrop of mixed signals: climate uncertainty weighs on the energy sector's long-term outlook, but regional tensions in the Middle East and Ukraine that disrupt refinery capacity could support oil prices and benefit producers in the near term. The stock's modest recovery today suggests investors are digesting the climate headline rather than fleeing energy stocks outright.
